title: Getting Help
about: Where to get help, what to save, and who to tell when things go wrong.

cards.prompt: You block a bully before saving their messages. What happens?

options.text: The messages may disappear, so there's nothing to show
The app keeps a copy for you to report later
options.nudge: Some apps hide or delete the chat once you block. Screenshot first, to be safe.

options.text: Blocking reports them to the app at the same time
options.nudge: Blocking only stops them reaching you. Reporting is a separate step.

options.text: Nothing changes: the messages stay in your chat
options.nudge: Not always. Some apps remove the chat when you block, so save it first.

cards.explanation: On some apps, blocking hides the chat, and the evidence goes with it. Screenshot first, then block.
cards.hint: After you block someone, can you always still see your chat with them?

cards.title: Never your fault
cards.body:
Scams and online cruelty happen to lots of people, even experts. **It's never your fault**, and telling someone is brave.

Before you block, **save the evidence**: screenshot the messages, the username, the web address and the date. A **private or nude image**? Don't save or share the image itself: write down the username and where it is, then report it.

cards.sentence: Outside your family, **Kids Helpline** (ages 5 to 25) is 1800 55 1800 and **Lifeline** is 13 11 14, any time.

cards.prompt: Worried online, but not ready to tell family. What now?

options.text: Call Kids Helpline, or talk to a school counsellor
Wait until it's bad enough to tell someone
options.nudge: You don't need a big problem to ask for help. Who could you talk to outside your family?

options.text: Ask strangers on an online forum
options.nudge: Strangers online aren't trusted adults, and some aren't who they say they are.

cards.explanation: Kids Helpline and a school counsellor are there for you. You don't have to wait, or cope alone.
cards.hint: The last card named people outside the family who can help.

cards.sentence: **Report** it in the app first, and report a scam to **Scamwatch** (scamwatch.gov.au) to warn others.

cards.prompt: People in a group chat post mean messages about you.

steps.text: It keeps going. What do you do first?

choices.text: Reply with something just as mean
choices.consequence: That usually makes things worse, and can get you in trouble too.

choices.text: Screenshot the messages, and tell a trusted adult
choices.consequence: Now you have evidence, and someone on your side.

choices.text: Delete the chat so you don't see it
choices.consequence: That deletes the evidence too. Save it first.

choices.text: Report it in the app, then block or leave
choices.consequence: The app can remove it. If not, eSafety can help.
Reporting gives the app, and eSafety, the chance to stop it.

cards.explanation: Don't reply. Save the evidence, tell a trusted adult, then report and block.
cards.hint: Think about the order: evidence and a trusted adult first, then reporting.

cards.sentence: If money's involved, tell **your bank** straight away; if details are stolen, **IDCARE** (idcare.org) helps.
If someone could get hurt right now, call **000**.

cards.prompt: Match each problem to where to go.
cards.explanation: Serious bullying goes to eSafety, card trouble to your bank, stolen details to IDCARE, and danger to 000.
cards.hint: Look back at the last two cards: what is each one for?
cards.nudge: Start with the one you're surest of. What is each service for?

cards.prompt: A scam used your card. You call your bank now. What happens?

options.text: They can block the card, and may stop the payment
Nothing: once money's gone, a bank can't do anything
options.nudge: Banks deal with scams every day. Calling fast gives them the best chance to help.

options.text: They tell you off for falling for a scam
options.nudge: You won't be in trouble. Scams fool adults too, and banks just want to help.

options.text: They wait a week to see if it happens again
options.nudge: Banks act fast on scams. That's why calling straight away matters.

cards.explanation: Calling fast, with an adult, lets the bank block the card and maybe stop the payment. You're not in trouble.
cards.hint: Why would the lesson say to tell your bank straight away?

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Never your fault:** tell a trusted adult, **Kids Helpline** (1800 55 1800) or **Lifeline** (13 11 14).
- Report in the app, then **eSafety** (esafety.gov.au), **Scamwatch**, your **bank**, or **000** if there's danger.
- **Try this:** save Kids Helpline and a trusted adult's number in your phone.

**Next:** the course challenge that brings every skill together.
